findings.title: Purged CV override is properly scoped via try/finally
findings.notes: The `try/finally` in the per-symbol block correctly saves `PHASE2_CV_FILTER_ENABLED` before override and restores it in the `finally` clause. This survives all exit paths: normal completion, per-symbol `continue` after exception, and propagated exceptions. Verified empirically: after `_run_phase2(force=True)`, `_cfg.PHASE2_CV_FILTER_ENABLED` returns to its original value.

findings.title: _tag_pool_with_symbol edge cases are handled correctly
findings.notes: Edge cases verified: (a) empty pool → empty list, (b) empty `conditions` list → `['symbol is S']` appended, (c) duplicate `symbol is X` condition → no-op (idempotent), (d) rule missing `conditions` key → treated as `[]` and tag is added, (e) input is not mutated (shallow copy via `dict(rule)` plus `list(...)` on conditions). Verified by running ad-hoc tests against the live code.

findings.title: Per-symbol exception handling is correct: failed symbol is skipped, others continue
findings.notes: Verified empirically: with three symbols A/B/C, B raises a RuntimeError, the pipeline logs the error with `exc_info=True`, skips B via `continue`, and successfully generates pools for A and C. Final merged pool has 2 rules. The pipeline does not abort. The outer direction-level `try/except` from the original code is intentionally not used here — this is a deliberate change in failure semantics (one bad symbol does not kill the whole direction), and it's what the task spec requested.

findings.title: Config values are reasonable and well-documented
findings.notes: PER_SYMBOL_PHASE2=True default matches the spec. PER_SYMBOL_MIN_ROWS=1000 is a reasonable floor for meaningful per-symbol training. PHASE2_PER_SYMBOL_POOL_DIR is derived from existing PHASE2_POOL_DIR (no hardcoded path). All three new constants have explanatory comments.

findings.title: No hardcoded paths
findings.notes: Per-symbol directory: `_cfg.PHASE2_PER_SYMBOL_POOL_DIR` (config-derived). Standard pool path: `_phase2_module._POOL_PATHS[direction]` (config-derived). Per-symbol file name: `f'phase2_{direction}_{symbol}_pool.json'` (uses loop/direction variables, no hardcoded literal). File output parent directories are created with `os.makedirs(..., exist_ok=True)`. Standard path's parent is also created defensively.

findings.title: Style consistency with project
findings.notes: Uses `getattr(_cfg, ..., default)` defensive pattern (consistent with rest of file). Numpy-style docstrings on the new helpers. f-strings for format. Same indentation, same logger usage, same exc_info=True style. The new `if per_symbol_phase2 / else` branch keeps the original combined-symbols path verbatim below it (not refactored), which preserves diff readability and matches the 'clean old implementation' guidance.

findings.title: Logging is informative and uses appropriate levels
findings.notes: INFO for progress (per-symbol start, generated count, merged total). WARNING for skip conditions (insufficient rows, GPU runtime failure). ERROR with `exc_info=True` for per-symbol failures. The final 'merged N rules from M symbols' line is informative. Direction name is included in every message via `dir_phase_name`.

findings.title: Memory/performance characteristics
findings.notes: Per-symbol loop does `train_df[train_df['symbol'] == symbol].copy()` which creates a full DataFrame copy per symbol. For typical symbol counts (single-digit to low double-digit) this is acceptable. The GPU runtime is reconfigured once per symbol (matching original per-direction pattern); this is non-trivial overhead but mirrors the existing code. No memory leak in the loop body.

findings.title: Possible suboptimal behavior: previous-pool seeding includes rules from other symbols
findings.notes: `Rule_Pool_Generator.run()` calls `Rule_Pool_Generator.load_pool(direction)` which loads the merged standard pool. On a re-run of per-symbol mode, this merged pool contains rules tagged with other symbols. These are then used as `seed_chromosomes` for the current symbol's evolution. Suboptimal but not breaking: chromosomes are valid regardless of symbol tag; the new rules for the current symbol are tagged correctly when merged back. The original combined-symbols mode has the same behavior, so this is consistent with the existing design rather than a regression.

findings.title: try/finally scope is appropriate
findings.notes: The `try/finally` only wraps the per-symbol loop, not the subsequent merge + standard-path write. This is correct: we want the config restored before doing other work. If the merge step or standard-path write raises, the exception propagates, which is consistent with the original combined-symbols behavior (an exception in `generator.run()` was logged but `pool = []` set; an exception during file write would have propagated too).

findings.title: No dead code, no unused imports
findings.notes: Both new helpers (`_tag_pool_with_symbol`, `_merge_pools`) are referenced. No new imports were added. The old `pool = []` initializer in the exception handler is gone with the original branch (the new branch has its own empty-pool path: all symbols skipped → empty `per_symbol_pools` → empty `merged_pool`). The original `else` branch (combined-symbols) keeps its old structure verbatim.

correctness.notes: All edge cases handled. Per-symbol path tested live: (a) symbols with insufficient rows are skipped with warning, (b) successful symbols contribute to merged pool with correct 'symbol is S' tag, (c) per-symbol exception is caught and logged with traceback, other symbols continue, (d) PHASE2_CV_FILTER_ENABLED is restored to its original value after the run. Backward compat verified by reading the `else` branch (combined-symbols path unchanged).

edge_cases.notes: Empty pool, empty conditions, duplicate conditions, missing 'conditions' key, all-symbols-fail, all-symbols-skipped (insufficient rows), and per-symbol exception paths all handled. The dedup in `_tag_pool_with_symbol` is via `any(str(c) == cond_str for c in conditions)`, which correctly handles both string and any-stringifiable entries.

test_adequacy.notes: The 8 existing tests in tests/unit/test_run_pipeline.py (verified by implementer) cover the broader pipeline but do not specifically cover the per-symbol path. The implementer's handoff states: 'helper functions verification: _tag_pool_with_symbol, _merge_pools: OK' — these were ad-hoc, not committed tests. I ran similar ad-hoc tests during review and they all pass. A committed unit test for `_tag_pool_with_symbol` and `_merge_pools` (and ideally for the try/finally CV restoration) would improve coverage. This is not blocking; the new helpers are small and exercised end-to-end in normal pipeline runs.

config_changes.notes: Three new config constants, all derived from existing values, all documented. PER_SYMBOL_PHASE2=True default matches task spec. PER_SYMBOL_MIN_ROWS=1000 is conservative. PHASE2_PER_SYMBOL_POOL_DIR uses os.path.join on the existing PHASE2_POOL_DIR (no hardcoded literal).

recommendation: APPROVED. The implementation is clean, well-scoped, follows project conventions, and handles all identified edge cases correctly. Minor suggestions (committed unit tests for the new helpers, documentation of why CV is disabled in per-symbol mode) are not blocking.
